output_json.patch_notes:
Root-cause fix at the shared trust boundary: added a private static helper `isFileWithinDestination(File destination, File file)` in ArchiveAnalyzer.java that resolves both paths via getCanonicalPath() and confirms `file` is the destination or a descendant of it (catching IOException as a fail-closed/false result). Applied this check:
1. In `extractArchive(ArchiveInputStream, File, Engine)` immediately after `final File file = new File(destination, entry.getName());` and before the directory-entry `mkdirs()` branch or the `engine.accept(file)` -> `extractAcceptedFile` branch — this single call site is shared by both ZIP-family (zip/jar/war/ear/sar/apk/nupkg via ZipArchiveInputStream) and TAR (via TarArchiveInputStream) extraction, so both are covered by one fix. Entries that fail the check are skipped with a WARN log and the loop continues to the next entry (does not abort the whole extraction).
2. In `extractFiles(File, File, Engine)` for the GZIP (`gz`/`tgz`) and BZIP2 (`bz2`/`tbz2`) single-file decompression branches, which independently build `new File(destination, uncompressedName)` from `GzipUtils.getUncompressedFilename`/`BZip2Utils.getUncompressedFilename` and were not covered by the extractArchive fix.
This blocks plain "../" traversal, nested "../../../" traversal, and absolute-path entry names (since an absolute `file` path will never be a descendant of the canonical destination path), across all archive types the analyzer supports, not just the ZIP path the POV exercised.
Added a JUnit regression test `testExtractFilesBlocksZipSlip` in ArchiveAnalyzerTest.java that builds a malicious ZIP with both a "../PWNED_outside_destination.txt" traversal entry and a normal "safe.txt" entry, invokes the real private `ArchiveAnalyzer.extractFiles` via reflection (mirroring the POV's approach), and asserts the traversal entry is never written outside the destination while the legitimate entry still extracts correctly into the destination.
Verified: `mvn -B -pl core compile` and `test-compile` succeed; `mvn -B -pl core -Dtest=ArchiveAnalyzerTest test` passes; re-running the provided POV (`bash .security-pipeline/pov/run_pov.sh`) against the patched code now prints "NOT VULNERABLE" and exits 1 (previously exited 0/vulnerable).
output_json.risk_notes: Low risk. The change only adds a containment check before existing filesystem operations; it does not alter behavior for well-formed archive entries (verified via the new test's "safe.txt" assertion). Entries that fail the check are silently skipped (with a WARN log) rather than aborting the whole extraction/analysis, which preserves availability for scanning legitimate archives that might incidentally contain one bad entry, at the cost of not surfacing a hard failure — this matches the existing error-tolerant style of extractArchive (IOException/AnalysisException are already caught and logged elsewhere in this pipeline). Canonicalization relies on File.getCanonicalPath(), which resolves symlinks; if the destination directory itself is expected to legitimately contain symlinks pointing outside of it for some other supported workflow, this fix would also block writes through those — no such usage was found in this codebase. Did not run the full `mvn -B test` suite (very large legacy reactor with heavy integration tests and network-dependent NVD/CVE data); scoped verification to compiling the whole core module and running the affected test class, which is sufficient to confirm the fix and no regression in the touched code paths.
output_json.summary: Fixed a Zip Slip / path traversal vulnerability (CWE-022) in ArchiveAnalyzer by validating that every archive entry's resolved output path stays within the extraction destination before any filesystem side effect (mkdirs or file write) occurs. The root cause was `new File(destination, entry.getName())` (ArchiveAnalyzer.java:516, now shifted a few lines due to the added check) being used without canonicalization/containment checks, letting a crafted entry name (e.g. "../PWNED_outside_destination.txt", absolute paths, or nested "../../.." sequences) escape the destination directory. Added a `isFileWithinDestination(File destination, File file)` helper that compares canonical paths, and applied it at the single shared choke point in `extractArchive` (covering both the directory-entry `mkdirs()` sink and the file-entry `extractAcceptedFile` -> `parent.mkdirs()`/`FileOutputStream` sinks, for both ZIP-family and TAR archives since they share this method), plus at the two additional entry points in `extractFiles` that independently build `new File(destination, uncompressedName)` for the GZIP and BZIP2 single-file decompression paths. Entries that would escape the destination are now skipped with a warning log instead of being extracted, while legitimate entries continue to extract normally.
